item.title: Israeli strike kills worker with UN Palestinian agency in Gaza, agency says
item.description:
CAIRO, Nov 23 (Reuters) - An Israeli airstrike killed a Gaza man working for the UN Palestinian refugee agency UNRWA in the Gaza Strip on Monday, the relief agency and local health officials said.

The man, whom medics named as Adel Al-Helo, was working near a water well in the Jabalia refugee camp in the enclave's north, UNRWA and medics said. Three others were wounded in the strike, they said.

item.title: Ukraine claims it sank Russian warship off Libya
item.description:
Ukraine on Monday claimed it was behind strikes on two Russian vessels off Libya, including one that sank a modern warship, in the latest spillover from Moscow's invasion. 

The attacks on Sunday near the Libyan port of Benghazi come at a time when Ukraine has stepped up its daring strikes against Russia far from the frontlines in retaliation for Moscow's deadly invasion.

Here is what we know about the attacks:  

 

- What do Libyan authorities say? -

item.title: Iran says it will use all its tools to confront US naval blockade
item.description:
DUBAI, Nov 23 (Reuters) - Iran will use all its tools to confront the US naval blockade, Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said in a weekly news conference on Monday.

The US blockade on Iran-related oil exports was imposed on April 13, lifted in June after Washington reached a draft understanding with Tehran, then restored on July 14 after the agreement collapsed.

"We will definitely not tolerate it (the blockade) and we will use all our tools to confront this US aggression," Baghaei said.

item.title: COP flop triggers backlash in Australia; Pacific nations express despair
item.description:
By Praveen Menon and Lewis Jackson

SYDNEY/ANTALYA, Turkey, Nov 23 (Reuters) - The finger pointing to assign blame for the collapse of UN climate talks in Turkey began on Monday with calls for the resignation of the Australian minister leading them, while the Pacific island nations most at risk expressed their despair over the failure of countries to collectively address global warming.

item.title: Bad COP, worse COP: What's next after climate talks fail?
item.description:
The collapse of marathon climate talks in Turkey has renewed questions about reform of their consensus requirement, and galvanised calls for legal action and ambitious side agreements between like-minded countries.

The "conference of the parties" talks, better known as COP31, ended without agreement and two days over schedule on Sunday, as countries deadlocked on fossil fuels, finance, science and carbon-removing technologies.

item.title: Saudi Arabia's influence loomed large over failed COP31 deal
item.description:
By Valerie Volcovici and Sarah McFarlane

ANTALYA, Turkey, Nov 23 (Reuters) - As the COP31 climate conference drifted into what proved to be record overtime, a negotiator from a small island state complained that a promised meeting with the talks' Turkish and Australian presidents had been cancelled yet again.

Saudi officials, meanwhile, had regular access, allowing them disproportionate influence at the Antalya conference, according to negotiators from Europe, small island states, Latin America, Asia and Africa.

item.title: Analysis-Can climate diplomacy build on the collapse of COP31?
item.description:
By Peter Hobson, Simon Jessop, Valerie Volcovici and Sarah McFarlane

ANTALYA, Turkey, Nov 23 (Reuters) - The collapse of COP31 talks in Turkey on Sunday without a political agreement left exhausted negotiators questioning the future of a process that for three decades has led the global fight against climate change.

For the small, vulnerable countries most exposed to rising sea levels and the increasingly extreme weather scientists link to rising carbon emissions, annual UN conferences are their chance to draw the world's attention to their plight and seek financial help.

item.title: Iran strike wounds two in Bahrain, Saudi condemns 'criminal' attacks
item.description:
Bahrain said Sunday that two people were wounded in an Iranian strike the previous day on "a civilian industrial site" in the Gulf kingdom, which has faced several attacks this week.

Iran's Revolutionary Guards have repeatedly said they targeted US facilities in Bahrain, where Iranian strikes resumed on November 13 after a lull since early September.

"In the wake of the criminal Iranian attacks suffered yesterday (Saturday) by the Kingdom of Bahrain... a Bahraini national with a disability was wounded," Bahrain's interior ministry said on X.

item.title: Libya's eastern government suspects drone attack caused explosion on Russian ship
item.description:
By Ayman Al-Warfali

Nov 22 (Reuters) - A suspected drone attack caused an explosion aboard a Russian ship docked at the Benghazi naval base in eastern Libya, the country's eastern-based government said on Sunday after a preliminary investigation.

No one has claimed responsibility for the suspected attack, and there was no immediate reaction from Russian authorities.

Since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, Ukrainian forces have repeatedly used naval drones and missiles to target Russian warships and naval facilities, mainly in the Black Sea.

item.title: Drone strikes hit homes, UN building in Sudan's capital
item.description:
Drones struck Sudan's capital Khartoum, ripping through homes and damaging a United Nations building on Sunday, witnesses and the world organisation said.

Explosions rang out in the area around Khartoum airport and other parts of the city from around 2:00 am (0000 GMT) until approximately 4:30 am.

A drone strike destroyed a house, a witness said, while a Sudanese army source said the drones had been launched from Ethiopia.

item.title: Netanyahu, Eisenkot parties end talks without deal on forming Israel govt
item.description:
The parties of caretaker Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his rival Gadi Eisenkot concluded a new round of talks on Sunday without reaching an agreement on a possible coalition government, which would require concessions from both sides.

Delegations from Eisenkot's Yashar party and Netanyahu's Likud met for four hours at a hotel in Herzliya, near Tel Aviv, following a first round of discussions last Sunday.

item.title: COP31 climate talks set to collapse without political deal
item.description:
ANTALYA, Turkey, Nov 22 (Reuters) - UN climate talks in Turkey looked set to collapse without a political agreement after COP31 summit president Murat Kurum said there would be no new draft of the deal.

Earlier, multiple countries and negotiating blocs said they could not accept the version of the text put before them.

"There will be no new text from now on. We will not be carrying out work on a new text in an environment where there is no consensus," Kurum said.

(Reporting by Tuvan Gumrukcu, writing by William James)

item.title: Israel's Eisenkot condemns arson attacks by Jewish settlers in West Bank
item.description:
By Ali Sawafta and Mohammed Torokman

RAMALLAH, Nov 22 (Reuters) - Israeli militant settlers attacked Palestinian villages in the occupied West Bank early on Sunday, starting fires and scrawling racist graffiti, residents said, prompting an accusation of "Jewish terrorism" from the man trying to form an Israeli government.

item.title: Dismay as chaotic UN climate talks collapse without a deal
item.description:
Climate advocates reacted with indignation on Monday to the COP31 summit ending in failure, with contentious talks collapsing over fossil fuels after the meeting in Turkey stretched into record overtime.

The final agreement was rejected on Sunday in a chaotic finale to the UN climate summit that ran two days over schedule, underscoring the strains on diplomacy in an increasingly fractured world.

item.title: Bahrain says Iran strikes industrial facility as air defences intercept attacks
item.description:
Nov 21 (Reuters) - Bahrain said an Iranian attack hit a civilian industrial facility on Saturday, while Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they had launched a missile-and-drone assault on US military positions in the kingdom, home to the US Navy's Fifth Fleet.

In a statement on Sunday, Bahrain's Interior Ministry said two people were injured in Iranian attacks on the country during the previous day - a Pakistani resident, who was in a critical condition, and a Bahraini citizen, who was stable.

item.title: Countries react as COP31 climate talks collapse
item.description:
ANTALYA, Turkey, Nov 22 (Reuters) - The COP31 conference in Turkey ended in collapse on Sunday after countries failed to agree an overarching political deal on how to tackle climate change.

Below are reactions from delegates:

ANTONIO GUTERRES, UNITED NATIONS SECRETARY GENERAL

"I am deeply disappointed that COP31 has ended without consensus on an overarching outcome. I share the very profound frustration of all those who expected governments to rise to the moment the climate crisis demands."

item.title: Bahrain says Iran struck industrial site as tankers hit in Hormuz
item.description:
Bahrain accused Iran of striking a civilian industrial facility on Saturday, causing a fire and damage but no casualties, while two tankers were hit in the Strait of Hormuz, at the heart of the Middle East conflict.

The Gulf kingdom has suffered several attacks this week, ending a weeks-long lull in the conflict that began with US-Israeli strikes on Iran in late February.

item.title: In an Egypt village, generations of Palestinians denied a normal life
item.description:
Shamma Abu Hussein is possibly the last person in her village of refugees to have lived in historic Palestine. Living in Egypt, she has watched three generations of her family grow up in legal limbo.

She was among the hundreds of thousands who fled or were expelled during the creation of the State of Israel in 1948, whose descendants number in the millions.

Now she fears that the effects of the Gaza war and rhetoric from Israeli ministers calling for Gazans to be expelled means history is repeating itself.

item.title: Syrian Christian town demands security after resident kidnapped
item.description:
When Amina saw her nephew's motorbike knocked onto the ground and a car speeding away from his home in central Syria, she thought there had been a crash.

Instead, 38-year-old jeweller Maher Sankari had been kidnapped, an incident that plunged the Christian town of Suqaylabiyah into fear and prompted church leaders to demand authorities take action against repeated attacks and kidnappings of Christians.

Sankari's captors are demanding an eye-watering ransom of 120 kilogrammes (265 pounds) of gold.

item.title: COP31 climate talks collapse as EU and others reject deal
item.description:
By Peter Hobson, Lewis Jackson and Ezgi Erkoyun

ANTALYA, Turkey, Nov 22 (Reuters) - UN climate talks ended in collapse on Sunday as the European Union and others rejected a final deal put forward by COP31 presidents Turkey and Australia, saying it was too weak to advance the fight against global warming.

The failed talks reflect the struggle by governments across the world to muster ambitious action to address the worsening consequences of climate change — including heatwaves, wildfires, floods and powerful storms — as wars and economic pressures compete for their attention.
